instruction:
You are a senior civil engineer specializing in road geometry and horizontal alignment design.

## Problem

Determine the required superelevation rate and superelevation development (runoff) length for a horizontal curve.

## Given

| Parameter | Value | Unit |
|-----------|-------|------|
| Design speed (V) | {{ design_speed_km_h }} | km/h |
| Curve radius (R) | {{ curve_radius_m }} | m |
{% if side_friction_factor is defined %}
| Side friction factor (f) | {{ side_friction_factor }} | - |
{% endif %}
| Lane width (w) | {{ lane_width_m }} | m |
{% if rotation_rate is defined %}
| Rotation rate | {{ rotation_rate }} | m/m |
{% endif %}
{% if archetype_description is defined %}

### Site Conditions

{{ archetype_description }}
{% endif %}

{% if tool_available %}
## Available Tool

A superelevation calculation tool is available at `/workspace/{{ meta.name }}_calc.py`. Run it with:

```bash
python3 /workspace/{{ meta.name }}_calc.py --help
```

You may use this tool to verify your calculations or compute values directly.
{% endif %}

## Required

Calculate the following:

1. Required superelevation rate e (%)
2. Superelevation development (runoff) length Ls (m)

## Applicable Standards

- Austroads Guide to Road Design Part 3 (AGRD Part 3 §7.5)
- AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets (Green Book)

## Constraints

- No internet access is available. Work from engineering knowledge and the provided tool.
- Use the point-mass equilibrium equation for superelevation:
  - e + f = V² / (127 × R)
  - Rearranged: e = V² / (127 × R) − f
  - where V is design speed in km/h, R is curve radius in m, f is side friction factor
  - e is a decimal fraction (e.g. 0.04 for 4%); report the result as a percentage
  - If the computed e is negative, clamp to 0 (curve is gentle enough for normal crown)
- Calculate development length using:
  - Ls = (e / 100) × w / rotation_rate
  - where e is superelevation rate (%), w is lane width (m), rotation_rate is the maximum rate of pavement rotation (m/m)
{% if rotation_rate is not defined %}
  - Use a default rotation rate of 0.005 (1:200) if not specified
{% endif %}

## Output Format

Show your step-by-step working in Markdown. At the end of your solution, include a JSON block with your final answers in exactly this format:

```json
{
  "superelevation_rate_pct": <numeric_value>,
  "development_length_m": <numeric_value>
}
```

Write your complete solution to `/workspace/output.md`.
paramsToml:
[meta]
name = "superelevation-rate"
description = "Superelevation rate and development length for horizontal curves using e + f = V^2 / (127 * R)"
long_description = "Determines the required superelevation rate and transition development length for horizontal road curves using the point-mass equilibrium equation e + f = V^2/(127*R) per AASHTO Green Book and Austroads AGRD Part 3 Section 7.5. Balances centripetal force demand between pavement banking and tyre side friction to ensure vehicle stability through curves."
discipline = "civil"
category = "horizontal-geometry"
standards = ["AGRD Part 3 §7.5", "AASHTO Green Book Ch. 3"]
tags = ["civil", "roads", "horizontal-geometry", "superelevation", "curves", "deterministic"]
tool_mode = "with-tool"

[params.design_speed_km_h]
type = "float"
unit = "km/h"
description = "Design speed V"
min = 60
max = 130

[params.curve_radius_m]
type = "float"
unit = "m"
description = "Horizontal curve radius R"
min = 50
max = 500

[params.side_friction_factor]
type = "float"
unit = "-"
description = "Side friction factor f"
min = 0.08
max = 0.19
derivable_from = "archetype"

[params.lane_width_m]
type = "float"
unit = "m"
description = "Lane width w"
min = 3.0
max = 4.5

[params.rotation_rate]
type = "float"
unit = "m/m"
description = "Maximum rate of pavement rotation (e.g. 1/200 = 0.005)"
min = 0.005
max = 0.01
default = 0.005
optional = true

# --- Outputs ---

[outputs.superelevation_rate_pct]
description = "Required superelevation rate e (%)"
tolerance = 0.03

[outputs.development_length_m]
description = "Superelevation development (runoff) length Ls (m)"
tolerance = 0.03

# --- Archetypes: road type / speed environment scenarios ---

[archetypes.rural_highway]
description = "Rural two-lane highway with moderate traffic and open terrain"
side_friction_factor = {min = 0.10, max = 0.14}
site_contexts = ["bruce-highway-qld", "princes-highway-vic", "great-western-highway-nsw"]

[archetypes.urban_arterial]
description = "Urban multi-lane arterial road with signalised intersections"
side_friction_factor = {min = 0.13, max = 0.17}
site_contexts = ["sydney-parramatta-road", "melbourne-hoddle-street", "brisbane-coronation-drive"]

[archetypes.freeway]
description = "High-speed divided freeway or motorway"
side_friction_factor = {min = 0.08, max = 0.12}
site_contexts = ["m1-pacific-motorway", "m2-hills-motorway", "western-ring-road-melbourne"]

[archetypes.mountain_road]
description = "Winding mountain road with tight curves and steep grades"
side_friction_factor = {min = 0.14, max = 0.19}
site_contexts = ["great-ocean-road-vic", "bells-line-of-road-nsw", "gillies-highway-qld"]

# --- Difficulty levels ---

[difficulty.easy]
description = "All parameters given, gentle curve on a rural highway"
visibility = "all_given"
archetypes = ["rural_highway", "freeway"]

[difficulty.medium]
description = "All parameters given, any road type and curve geometry"
visibility = "all_given"
archetypes = ["rural_highway", "urban_arterial", "freeway", "mountain_road"]

[difficulty.hard]
description = "Side friction factor hidden — agent must infer f from road type and design speed"
visibility = "partial"
hidden_params = ["side_friction_factor"]
replacement_text = "The road is a {{ archetype.description }} ({{ archetype.site_context }})"
archetypes = ["rural_highway", "urban_arterial", "freeway", "mountain_road"]
